title: Emberline daily promo spot: grade eight mixed-light key frames to one show white point off the in-frame grey card, then author the thumbnail/promo-card pack as a one-card-per-frame merge
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a daily promotional-spot turnaround: a public-facing channel drops 'fresh promotional footage' into a shared drive each afternoon and wants same-day 'tasteful colour correction', a polished screen-ready deliverable, the occasional caption line, and a 'lively and accessible, nothing overly corporate' house look, all handed back in the daily folder within 24 hours. The real post named a specific creator's channel and its editing app; here every real name is laundered to a fictional daily food-and-craft streaming show, 'Emberline', whose finishing producer is the unnamed client, and no real person, brand, product, marketplace, school or software (including any editing/colour/layout application) is named in any task-facing field. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the brief's literal core (a full timeline edit — trim/sequence/transitions/export + an editable project file) is NOT a connector capability, and the original benchmark spec both leaned on deprecated tone tools and amputated the stated five-frame batch to a single fully-graded hero (the other frames were stamped with one identical 'recipe', which is professionally wrong and deletes the only measurable thing — cross-frame match), while shipping the 'thumbnail' as a subject-on-a-solid-plate with no type set (a designed artifact punted away from the tool). The corrected design keeps the job the brief actually rewards — the same-day promo FINISHING package a colourist/finisher hands back alongside the in-house cut — and routes it to what the connectors genuinely do: the producer exported EIGHT representative key frames from today's spot, each shot across the day under its own mixed light with an 18% grey card clipped at the frame edge, and the freelancer grades all eight to ONE show look (each neutralized to its own in-frame card so the set is checkable), preps them for the card window without upscaling, vectorizes the show wordmark, and DATA-MERGES a genuinely hand-authored single-record promo/thumbnail-card template (one card per frame) into a screen-and-press-ready PDF — plus a short social teaser cut of the day's take and a caption seed. Nothing is invented beyond the brief's stated sub-tasks (colour correction across the day's frames, a channel thumbnail from the hero, a short social teaser, a caption line, same-day folder handback).
one_line_ask: Take today's eight exported promo key frames — each shot across the day under its own mixed light with an 18% grey card clipped in-frame — grade every one to a single lively-but-clean show look where each frame's grey card lands truly neutral at one common white point (each frame needs its own white-balance and exposure decision because each was lit differently), prep each to the card window without enlarging past the 4K source, vectorize the show wordmark, then data-merge the channel's authored single-record promo/thumbnail-card template into a one-card-per-frame PDF with the episode titles typeset and the wordmark crisp in every masthead — plus a short social teaser cut and a caption seed — all dropped in the dated daily folder same day.
full_brief:
Emberline is an independent daily food-and-craft streaming show and every afternoon our raw promo footage lands in the shared drive; the finished, post-ready package has to go back in the same dated folder within 24 hours. We do NOT need the spot itself edited here — our in-house editor cuts the timeline. What we need from you is the finishing package built off what we hand you.

Here is what you are given: (1) EIGHT representative key frames the editor exported from today's spot (a close-up sign-on, a pour, two people on the floor, a wide room, a crema detail, a hands-at-the-counter beat, the product shelf, and a to-camera sign-off), each a full 4K still. They were shot at different points across the afternoon under different mixed light — window, tungsten, and blown daylight all trade off — so straight out of the export they do NOT match each other: some read warm and dim, others cool and bright. To make the match checkable we clipped a photographic 18% grey card to the edge of frame on every one of the eight, and it stays in shot. A couple of frames also came off the rig not perfectly level. (2) emberline_promocard_template — the promo/thumbnail card page we hand-built, one card per page, with our real placeholder fields and two image slots (the 16:9 frame window and the wordmark masthead). (3) emberline_promo_schedule — our eight-card list: the episode number, the on-card title, a short segment label, the air date and the format tag for each of the eight cards we want in the pack. (4) emberline_wordmark_flat — our flat show wordmark on transparency, which we want razor-sharp on every card masthead. (5) emberline_promo_take — the day's single continuous long take (the presenter talking to camera plus room ambience) that the teaser and caption come from.

What I need back:
- THE THUMBNAIL / PROMO-CARD PACK (the main deliverable): a screen-and-press-ready PDF of our daily promo cards, ONE card per page, EIGHT pages, that our channel manager posts and our print vendor can run. For each of the eight frames, grade it, drop it into the card's 16:9 window with its episode number, title, segment label and air date bound in from the list, and our wordmark crisp in the masthead. The lead card (page one) is our hero — lift the on-camera subject so it pops as a clickable thumbnail while the rest of the frame's grade stays put.
- THE GRADE (this is the whole craft of it): the pack has to read as ONE show, not eight stills from eight different shoots. Bring every frame to the SAME house look — lively and accessible, warm and clean, nothing corporate — where the neutral grey card in that frame lands truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at ONE common white point and the set shares one exposure feel. Because each frame was lit differently, no two start from the same cast or brightness, so getting all eight onto that one white point is a per-frame decision — each frame has to be neutralized to its OWN in-frame grey card, and how far and which way to move is yours to judge from that card, frame by frame. A set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will drift apart at the grey cards and we will reject it. Do not blow the speculars on glass, foam or the windows, and do not crush the shadows to mud. When you are done, hand back, per frame, the white-balance (temperature / tint) and exposure move you dialed and the final pixel size, so we can confirm the pack was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.
- FRAME QUALITY: any frame that came off the rig tilted has to be levelled before it goes in the window — a crooked frame in the card looks broken and we will reject it. And each card window needs real resolution: the window is 16:9 and at post-and-print scale it needs at least ~2560 x 1440 px of actual image. The frames are 4K, so a 16:9 crop off the full frame clears that with room — do NOT grade on a small proxy or enlarge a frame to fill the window; anything under the floor prints and streams soft.
- THE WORDMARK: our flat wordmark cleaned to a crisp vector for the card masthead and reusable on future cards.
- THE TEASER + CAPTION: a short social teaser cut from the day's single long take for the launch post, and a short auto-generated content summary of that take to seed the post caption and description.

Keep the sources in our Creative Cloud folder and drop the finished package in a dated daily folder. Bind the episode numbers, titles, segment labels and air dates verbatim from the schedule — do not rename our cards. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the eight cards matched to one white point with the per-frame moves reported; every card frame at least ~2560 x 1440 px; every tilted frame levelled; the wordmark crisp vector on every masthead; exactly one card page per schedule row; plus the teaser and the caption seed.

inputs.name: keyframe_hero.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal still frame exported from a promotional video, raw unretouched export look: candid close-up of a mid-30s show presenter laughing mid-sentence to camera in a sunlit artisan coffee-roastery set, native 4K (3840x2160, 16:9), mixed warm tungsten key that reads slightly warm and a touch underexposed and flat, real skin pores and flyaway hairs, shallow depth of field with a busy blurred shelf-and-equipment background, documentary not glossy, natural grain, the whole frame rotated about 4 degrees off-level (horizon tilted), a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped to the set dressing at the FAR-LEFT edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text or captions, no real brand names or logos on any object.
inputs.realism_notes: The HERO and the frame that establishes the show look; it is also the lead thumbnail (page one) whose on-camera subject gets a masked selective lift. TWO planted decisions live only here: (a) it is rotated ~4deg off-level, so image_auto_straighten (the ONLY rectify path) must run before the card crop or the card prints crooked — the brief states the goal ('levelled') but not which frames; (b) its cast is warm-and-underexposed, so its correction toward the common white point is a COOL-and-lift move. The grey card sits at the FAR-LEFT so it survives the neutralization and is then cropped away when the 16:9 window is taken. Declared at 4K camera scale so a 16:9 card crop clears the ~2560x1440 floor without upscaling. Real frame-grab softness, not a posed studio portrait.

inputs.name: keyframe_pour.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: medium shot of the same show set, a hand pouring roasted beans from a scoop, cool window daylight that reads distinctly cool and a little dim, busy real-world background, candid documentary style, natural skin and bean texture, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool-and-dim frame: the correct move toward the common white point is the OPPOSITE of the hero — WARM the white balance and lift a touch. A blanket 'warm everything' or 'cool everything' pass fails across the set. Card at frame edge, cropped out of the final window. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_duo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: two people chatting over a roasting machine on the same set, mixed window-plus-tungsten light that reads near-neutral but flat and low-contrast, real textures, candid documentary style, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral cast: only a SMALL white-balance nudge to seat its card on the common white point — over-correcting pushes it off the set. The real work here is tonal (add contrast to match the set's feel without clipping). Tests that the agent reasons per frame rather than repeating a big correction. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_wide.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: wide environment shot of the roastery set interior with customers, large windows blowing out bright, cool afternoon cast, documentary style, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool cast AND blown window highlights: the correct grade warms the white balance toward the target, pulls the bright windows back so they hold instead of clipping, and still lands the card neutral. Highlight protection dominates. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_detail.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: macro detail of a finished latte with rosetta crema art on a wooden counter on the same set, shallow depth of field, cool mixed light that is also a touch bright, bright specular glints on the wet foam and glass, real foam micro-texture, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool and bright with hot speculars on foam/glass: warm the white balance toward the target, pull exposure down, and protect the blown-risk speculars. Its bright crema is a sensitive check for residual cast at the common white point. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_counter.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: hands working an espresso tamp at the counter on the same set, warm low tungsten light that reads warm and clearly underexposed / dark, real hand and metal texture, natural grain, the frame slightly off-level (horizon tilted a few degrees), a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: SECOND planted tilt (a few degrees off-level) plus the biggest EXPOSURE lift in the set — warm-and-dark, so cool the cast slightly and lift the shadows the most without going muddy or noisy, AND straighten it before the card crop. Two frames tilted (this and the hero) so 'straighten the tilted ones' is a genuine per-frame decision, not a single obvious one. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_shelf.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: the retail product shelf on the same set, bags and mugs on timber shelving, even neutral light that reads close to correct but flat and slightly low-contrast, real packaging and timber texture, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text, no legible real brand names on the packaging.
inputs.realism_notes: Already close to neutral: the smallest white-balance move of the set, the work is contrast/tone to match the house feel. Sits near the target so the trap is OVER-correcting it. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: keyframe_portrait.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 4K (3840x2160) video key frame, raw export look: the presenter to-camera sign-off on the same set, backlit by the window so the frame is hazy, flat and low-contrast with a slight warm cast, real skin texture and flyaways, natural grain, a small neutral photographic 18% grey card clipped at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no on-screen text.
inputs.realism_notes: Backlit, hazy and slightly warm: cut the haze with contrast, cool the slight warmth and lift carefully so its card lands neutral without crushing the flat backlit tone. Another distinct direction from the rest. 4K camera scale.

inputs.name: emberline_promo_take.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CAMERA ORIGINAL (declared at camera scale and real length; no generative video model produces this reliably, which is the point): a single continuous ~3 minute 4K (3840x2160, 16:9, ~24-30fps) hand-held-steady take on the same roastery set — the presenter talking to camera about the day's spot (clear speech), intercut naturally by the same continuous move with beans pouring, espresso pulling, crema settling and customers chatting in the room (room ambience and chatter audible), warm-to-cool mixed daylight drifting across the take, real documentary product-video look, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions, no real brand names or logos on any object.
inputs.realism_notes: ONE genuine ~3 minute 4K take, longer than any target derived from it, so video_create_quick_cut can SHORTEN it to a ~15s social teaser (the AI picks the cut — a tool decision, not an agent-owned one) and media_summarize can seed the caption from real on-camera speech + room ambience. Declared at camera scale/length so nothing upscales or is assembled/lengthened; it is a shorten-one-longer-take source, never a multi-clip assembly and never an ~8s AI clip.

inputs.name: emberline_promocard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 landscape (210 x 148 mm) daily promo / thumbnail card page with 3 mm bleed — ONE card per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<EpisodeNo>>, <<Title>>, <<Segment>>, <<AirDate>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 16:9 frame window (~200 x 113 mm, bleeding at the top) bound to @Frame (the graded card frame for that row), and a small masthead lockup frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized show wordmark). The <<Title>> text frame sits in a title-safe band over the lower-left of the image window and has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long episode title binds without going overset; <<EpisodeNo>>, <<Segment>> and <<AirDate>> sit in the caption strip. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is not available, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through the second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The card furniture (caption strip, title band, page ground) is already drawn into the template and is fixed on every page, so the only per-row imagery is the frame window and the masthead wordmark. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up contact sheet: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-record-per-page sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-card-per-page template is the correct, connector-doable shape (eight rows => an eight-page pack), not a multi-up sheet. Supplied as an input, never a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@Frame, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded card frame AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the agent-produced marks have a real, connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement. Column names must exactly match the schedule headers.

inputs.name: emberline_promo_schedule.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: EpisodeNo,Title,Segment,AirDate,@Frame,@Wordmark and 8 rows, one per promo card, in card order. EpisodeNo is a label string like 'EP-142'. Title is the human on-card episode title and MUST include at least one deliberately LONG title (e.g. 'The Afternoon Roast — Behind the Counter with the Whole Crew', ~54+ chars) alongside short ones (e.g. 'Sign On', 'The Pour') so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. Segment is a short NON-DIAGNOSTIC label naming only the beat or topic (e.g. 'Cold Open', 'The Pour', 'On the Floor', 'Wide Room', 'Crema Detail', 'At the Counter', 'The Shelf', 'Sign-Off') — it MUST NOT name any lighting cast, colour temperature, exposure, tilt or grade direction, so the correction stays the freelancer's decision from the grey card rather than a value read off the CSV. AirDate is a client-supplied label string (e.g. '2026-09-01') the agent binds verbatim, NOT a value the agent measures or computes. @Frame holds the agreed prepped card-frame filename for that row (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_08_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded frame into that card. @Wordmark holds 'emberline_wordmark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized masthead lockup binds onto every page). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<EpisodeNo>>,<<Title>>,<<Segment>>,<<AirDate>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight card pages (page-count = row-count gate). The @Frame column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those EXACT names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned masthead lands on every page. Title/Segment/AirDate are client copy bound verbatim. Crucially the CSV encodes NO treatment: Segment is topic-only (never a cast or exposure), there is no 'type' column, and every @Frame is the same .jpg extension — nothing in the client-supplied file tells the agent which frame is warm, cool, bright or tilted; that is decided from each frame's own in-frame grey card. The long title exercises the auto-fit frame.

inputs.name: emberline_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat minimalist show wordmark on a TRANSPARENT background: the word 'EMBERLINE' in an elegant high-contrast serif with a small ember/flame glyph above the I, solid single-colour (warm charcoal) glyphs, crisp clean hard edges, high contrast, centred with a generous transparent margin all around, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, exported slightly oversized and off-centre, 2600x700 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, single-colour text art on transparent alpha so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds to strip the generous transparent margin, then a crisp contrast pass so the edges separate hard). Text-bearing wordmark -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms. It is a SUPPLIED asset only cleaned and vectorized, never a from-scratch designed letterform.

outputs.name: EMBERLINE_DailyPromo_ThumbnailCards_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED DELIVERABLE. A screen-and-press-ready ~300 DPI A5 landscape (210 x 148 mm) + 3 mm bleed promo/thumbnail-card PDF, ONE card per page, EIGHT pages (page-count = schedule row-count = 8), exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge. Each page binds its EpisodeNo/Title/Segment/AirDate verbatim from the schedule, drops that row's grey-card-neutralized, house-graded card frame into the 16:9 window (>=2560 x 1440 px so it prints >=300 DPI and streams >=1080p), and drops the vectorized wordmark into the masthead lockup. The pack reads as ONE continuous show grade across all eight pages; page one is the hero card, its on-camera subject lifted so it pops as a clickable thumbnail. The 'hero' is simply page one of the merged pack (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the popped lead subject, the typeset titles, the crisp masthead — is the agent's, not a template default.

outputs.name: promo_frame_masters_cardbearing_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized full-frame masters (native ~3840x2160), one per key frame, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven to a clean neutral and the whole set matched to ONE shared white point and one exposure feel while the look stays lively and clean (warm, not corporate; bright, not blown; shadows deep, not muddy), and any tilted frame straightened. The grey card is RETAINED in frame in these masters — this is the grade-audit artifact the grader checks neutrality on (the card is cropped out of the card frames, so neutrality is graded HERE, on the retained card-bearing masters, not on the delivered pack). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each frame.

outputs.name: promo_card_frames_x8
outputs.spec: Eight 16:9 card frames (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_08_final.jpg), each cropped from the FULL-resolution card-bearing master to the card window's 16:9 ratio with the grey card cropped OUT, held at >=2560 x 1440 px (target ~3200 x 1800, downscaled from the 4K frame, never upscaled) so each prints >=300 DPI in the window and streams >=1080p. These are the @Frame assets the merge resolves per row; card-exclusion is checked HERE, separately from the neutrality check on the masters. frame_01_final is cropped from the hero master AFTER its masked subject pop.

outputs.name: emberline_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat show wordmark cleaned and vectorized to a crisp SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds then a crisp contrast pass then trace), razor-sharp at any size, bound into every card masthead via the @Wordmark column and reusable on future cards.

outputs.name: promo_teaser_15s.mp4
outputs.spec: A short (~15s) social teaser cut from the day's single ~3 minute 4K take for the launch post, produced by video_create_quick_cut [A] — the AI picks the highlight cut (a tool decision, a secondary deliverable, NOT the agent-owned endpoint). Output duration < source; the take is only SHORTENED, never assembled or lengthened. Frame-accurate editorial, text overlays and motion graphics are the in-house timeline finish, not claimed here.

outputs.name: caption_summary.txt
outputs.spec: A short auto-generated content summary of the day's take (media_summarize [A], pointed at the real AV asset with the presenter's to-camera speech and room chatter) to seed the post caption and description copy. A text deliverable derived from the video, never pointed at a document.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (NOT the primary output; the card pack is): for each of the eight frames, the white-balance temperature and tint and the exposure move that were applied, plus the final pixel size of each card frame, plus the single common show white point all eight were matched to, plus which frames required straightening. This makes 'the pack is matched to one target' checkable — the corrections must be non-identical across the warm-dim and cool-bright frames. It is an applied-settings log, never a measured/recovered pixel readout.

outputs.name: daily_delivery_YYYY-MM-DD/
outputs.spec: A dated CC asset folder containing all of the above (the card-pack PDF, the eight card-bearing masters, the eight card frames, the wordmark SVG, the teaser, the caption seed and the grade report), organized for same-day handback.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: keyframe_hero.jpg, keyframe_pour.jpg, keyframe_duo.jpg, keyframe_wide.jpg, keyframe_detail.jpg, keyframe_counter.jpg, keyframe_shelf.jpg, keyframe_portrait.jpg, emberline_wordmark_flat.png, emberline_promo_take.mp4
connector_workflow.note: Bring today's eight exported key frames, the flat show wordmark and the day's long take into the working project in one load so the grade, the logo cleanup and the teaser/caption can run against real asset references. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.

Level the lead frame if it came off the rig not perfectly level, BEFORE any grade or crop — image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt; a crooked frame dropped into the card window is rejected. The agent decides by eye which frames need this; not every frame does.

ESTABLISH the show house look on the lead frame and record it as the target the other seven must hit: using the in-frame 18% grey card as the reference, dial temperature and tint until that card reads truly neutral (no residual cast) at the common white point, then set exposure/highlights/shadows/whites/blacks/clarity/vibrance to the lively, accessible, not-corporate feel — bright not blown, shadows deep not muddy. Reason the direction and amount from THIS frame's card; report the move. Card RETAINED in frame — this is the card-bearing master. A reasoned primitive-built grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone.
Select the on-camera subject on the graded lead frame to drive a selective lift for the thumbnail pop. Semantic subject selection (allowed); returns a mask URI.

Masked selective edit: apply a small exposure/clarity/vibrance lift to the subject ONLY, using step 4's mask, so the presenter reads off the busy background for a clickable lead thumbnail while the surround grade set in step 3 is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine LOCAL edit — not a whole-image push, not a solid fill, not a whole-image overlay. Card still retained; this stays the hero card-bearing master.

Crop the grey card OUT and reframe the popped hero to the card's 16:9 window, taken from the FULL 3840x2160 master so it holds >=2560x1440 (target ~3200x1800). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only — never a canvas extend, never an enlarge past source. Report final px. Uploaded later as frame_01_final.jpg.

Grade this key frame to the SAME target set in step 3, neutralizing its OWN in-frame 18% grey card to the common white point and matching the set's exposure feel. Because this frame was lit differently, the direction and amount are its own decision read from its card, not the hero's numbers copied — a blanket correction across the set fails at the cards. Primitive-built grade (temperature/tint/exposure/highlights/shadows/whites/blacks/clarity), not a preset, not auto-tone. Report the move; card retained.

Crop the grey card OUT and reframe to the card's 16:9 window from the full master at >=2560x1440 (target ~3200x1800). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never upscale. Report final px. frame_02_final.jpg.

Grade this key frame to the common target, neutralizing its own in-frame grey card to the shared white point and matching the exposure feel. Judge the direction and amount from this frame's card — some frames need only a small nudge and over-correcting pushes them off the set. Primitive-built grade, not a preset, not auto-tone. Report the move; card retained.
Crop the grey card OUT and reframe to the card's 16:9 window from the full master at >=2560x1440. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never upscale. Report final px. frame_03_final.jpg.

Grade this key frame to the common target, neutralizing its own in-frame grey card to the shared white point and matching the exposure feel, and protect any blown-risk highlights so bright areas hold instead of clipping. Judge from this frame's card. Primitive-built grade, not a preset, not auto-tone. Report the move; card retained.
Crop the grey card OUT and reframe to the card's 16:9 window from the full master at >=2560x1440. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never upscale. Report final px. frame_04_final.jpg.

Grade this key frame to the common target, neutralizing its own in-frame grey card to the shared white point and matching the exposure feel; protect any specular glints on glass/foam while landing the card neutral. Judge from this frame's card. Primitive-built grade, not a preset, not auto-tone. Report the move; card retained.
Crop the grey card OUT and reframe to the card's 16:9 window from the full master at >=2560x1440. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never upscale. Report final px. frame_05_final.jpg.

Level this key frame if it came off the rig tilted, BEFORE grading and cropping — image_auto_straighten is the only rectify path. The agent decides by eye which frames need this (more than one frame in the set is off-level, and most are not); a crooked frame in the card window is rejected.

Grade this key frame to the common target, neutralizing its own in-frame grey card to the shared white point and matching the exposure feel; this is the frame most in need of a tonal recovery, so lift the shadows the most without going muddy or noisy while its card lands neutral. Judge from this frame's card. Primitive-built grade, not a preset, not auto-tone. Report the move; card retained.

difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon color_grade_lr finishing package scoped from the real daily-promo brief's connector-supported sub-tasks: 32 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image raster/colour [C], video/media [C]/[A], page-layout merge [T]/[C]) — well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the two upload idioms and the folder create (3 plumbing calls), leaving 29 difficulty-bearing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: the core is EIGHT different reasoned grade decisions, in different directions, all forced to converge on one measurable target (each frame's static in-frame 18% grey card at one common white point) even though every frame was lit differently — warm-dim frames cooled and lifted, cool-bright frames warmed and pulled down, near-neutral frames nudged only slightly, the darkest frame given the biggest tonal recovery, speculars and blown windows protected — so a blanket batch correction or per-frame auto-tone visibly fails to match at the cards. Layered on top: a masked subject-only lift on the hero (select_subject -> masked image_apply_adjustments) that must pop the presenter WITHOUT lifting the surround grade; a straighten decision the agent makes by eye on the two tilted frames (image_auto_straighten is the only rectify path); a camera-scale constraint (the 16:9 card window can only be met by a downscale crop from the full 3840x2160 frame, never an upscale); prep-before-trace wordmark discipline (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> vectorize); and a two-image-column one-file-per-row merge into a hand-authored single-record template that actually typesets the episode titles and binds the wordmark onto every masthead. It stays strictly inside connector limits: no timeline edit / project-file export, quick_cut only shortens the one longer take (no assembly/lengthen), no upscale, no generative fill/expand/text-to-image/compositing, image_fill_area and whole-image color_overlay are not used, no >90deg hsl rotation, convert_pdf_to_indd is not used, and the merge places one record per page (no N-up). Deprecated tone tools (image_adjust_color_temperature/_dark_portions/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast) are all replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the eight promo cards must read as ONE continuous show grade — every frame's in-frame 18% grey card driven to one common white point with the set on one exposure feel — and because every frame was lit differently, each needs its OWN, sometimes opposite, correction; running one global correction or per-frame auto-tone (which keys off each frame's own histogram) leaves the warm-dim and cool-bright frames disagreeing at the grey cards and the pack is rejected, and the agent must REPORT the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure move and final pixel size so 'matched' is auditable rather than asserted. A second decision gate is the straighten call: two frames came off the rig tilted and look otherwise like the rest, so the agent must catch them by eye and rectify with image_auto_straighten before the card crop — miss one and that card prints crooked. Two further checkable gates back it: every card frame must clear >=2560x1440 px (prints >=300 DPI in the 16:9 window / streams >=1080p) and the merged PDF page-count must equal the schedule row-count (8), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable common white point across eight differently-lit frames, each requiring a different, sometimes opposite correction reasoned to its own retained grey card — not one set of sliders; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — a masked subject-only lift that pops the lead without breaking the surround grade, a 16:9 card frame that can only come from a downscale crop of the full 4K frame with no upscaling permitted, and prep-before-trace wordmark discipline; plus a real merge that typesets the titles and binds the agent-produced wordmark onto every masthead. TRAP (the brief and the CSV disclose NONE of it — the brief states the goal 'the pack has to read as one show' and the schedule's Segment column is topic-only, no cast/exposure/tilt, no type column, every @Frame the same .jpg): the naive path auto-tones or globally corrects each frame so each looks fine alone, which passes a thumbnail but drifts apart at the grey cards and fails the one-white-point gate; a second pitfall is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference) — which is why neutrality is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing masters and card-exclusion is checked separately on the card frames; a third is grading on a downscaled proxy or enlarging a frame to fill the window, dropping under the resolution floor; a fourth is failing to straighten the two tilted frames. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, agent never measures): every grey card neutral (R=G=B) at the common white point on the eight retained masters with per-frame WB/exposure reported; every card frame >=2560x1440 px with final px reported; both tilted frames straightened; the wordmark a crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one screen-and-press-ready ~300 DPI card page per schedule row, page one the popped hero.
